privacyContent.intro: Unutma is a personal assistant and organizer that runs on your phone. There is no account and no Unutma server that stores what you enter. This policy explains what the app keeps on your device, the few cases in which something leaves your device, and what reaches us: emails you choose to send us, and the technical details that any internet request carries.
privacyContent.noPersonalDataText: We do not collect your personal data. Your tasks, notes, lists, routines, calendar, expenses, journal, vault, assistant conversations and settings are stored only on your device, and we have no access to them. Apart from the technical details that any internet request carries (section 7), the only information that reaches us is an email you decide to send (section 12).
privacyContent.dataOnDevice: 2. Data on your device, backups and deletion
privacyContent.dataOnDeviceText:
Everything you enter is stored in the app's private storage on your device. If you set a display name, it also stays on your device. On iPhone and iPad, if you back up your whole device to iCloud or a computer, iOS includes the app's data in that backup, as it does for other apps. On Android the app's data is excluded from Google's automatic backup.

Backups are optional. You can export a backup file protected with a password you choose and keep or send it wherever you like (for example iCloud Drive, Google Drive, email or your phone's storage). If you turn on automatic backup, the app saves password-protected copies in its own folder on your device. A backup file stays between you and the place you keep it; we never receive it. The vault is not part of the main backup and has its own separate backup. The assistant's personal facts are included in the backup; its chat history, learned corrections, search index and saved contacts are not.

"Delete all data" in the app, or uninstalling the app, removes your data from this device. We have no copy, so we cannot restore it.
privacyContent.assistantText:
The assistant files what you type or say in the right place and answers questions from your own records. It runs entirely on your device, using built-in rules and a small language-understanding model that is part of the app. The model is not downloaded from the internet, and the assistant does not use any online AI service. What you type and the assistant's answers are not sent anywhere. The assistant is available in Turkish, English, German, Spanish, French and Italian.

On your device, in encrypted form, the assistant keeps: your chat history; personal facts you tell it (for example your blood type or licence plate) so it can answer later; corrections it learns from you; a search index built from your records; and the "Misunderstood" list of sentences you mark.

Chat history is kept for 30 days by default. You can choose 7 days, 30 days, forever or "Don't keep" (the chat then exists only while the app is open). Shortening the period deletes older messages immediately. Under Settings > "Privacy and stored data" you can see how much of each is stored and delete it.
privacyContent.voiceInputText:
Voice input is optional; you can always type instead. When you tap the microphone, the app uses your phone's own speech recognition (Apple on iPhone and iPad, Google on Android) to turn your voice into text. The app does not save recordings.

"On-device recognition only" is on by default: your voice is recognized on the phone and does not go to a server. If your phone cannot recognize your language offline, the app asks you before using the phone's online speech service. If you allow it, Apple or Google may process your audio on their servers under their own privacy terms. Nothing is sent to us. You can change this at any time under Settings > "Privacy and stored data".

Spoken answers use your phone's built-in text-to-speech; the app does not pick voices that need the internet. The short fixed phrases the assistant plays are pre-recorded clips included in the app.
privacyContent.contacts: 5. Contacts and sending to other people
privacyContent.contactsText:
The app looks at your contacts only when you tap "Pick from contacts" to send something, such as a shopping list or a task, to someone. On iPhone the system contact picker opens and the app receives only the person you tap; no contacts permission is needed. On Android the app first asks for permission to read contacts and then opens the system picker. The app never reads or copies your whole contact list.

For the person you pick, or someone you tell the assistant about (for example "my sister's number is ..."), the app keeps only the name, one phone number, the relationship you mentioned and how you last sent to them (WhatsApp, SMS or share). This is stored encrypted on your device so you don't have to pick again, and the number is shown partly hidden on screen. These saved people are removed with "Delete all data" or when you uninstall the app. You can also delete them one by one, or all at once, in Settings > Privacy and stored data > Saved people.

Unutma never sends a message by itself. When you tap Send, it opens WhatsApp, your SMS app or the share menu with the message filled in; you send it from there, and that app's terms apply. If you share a task as a link, the task travels inside the link itself (after the # sign) and is not stored on our website's server.
privacyContent.permissionsText:
The app asks for a permission only when you use a feature that needs it; everything else works without it.

Notifications: reminders are scheduled on your device. There is no push server. The only notifications that do not come from your own entries are urgent announcements (section 7), and you can turn them off.

Microphone and speech recognition: only for voice input (section 4).

Contacts: only for "Pick from contacts" (section 5).

Face ID, Touch ID or fingerprint: to open the vault and past journal entries. Your phone performs the check; the app only learns whether it succeeded.

Photos: if you add a photo to a journal entry, the app may ask for access to your photos; a copy of the photo you choose is kept in the app's storage on your device.

Alarms (Android): when you ask for a phone alarm, the app opens your Clock app with the time and title filled in.

Widgets: home-screen and lock-screen widgets open the app. On Android the home-screen widget can show your quick actions, when you last logged them and today's journal mood, so anyone who sees your home screen can see them too.

Sharing into Unutma (Android): text you share to Unutma from another app opens in Unutma so you can save it.
privacyContent.network: 7. When the app uses the internet
privacyContent.networkText:
There is no Unutma server that receives your data. The app goes online only in these cases:

App updates: when the app starts, it asks Expo's update service (EAS Update, operated by 650 Industries, Inc.) whether a fix is available for your app version. The request contains only technical details: the platform (iOS or Android), the app version and a random identifier created by the update software to tell installations apart. As with any internet connection, Expo can see your IP address. The request contains none of your content.

Announcements: at most once every 24 hours, when you open the app, it downloads a public file with announcements from our website (unutma-blog.vercel.app), for example an urgent service notice or a feedback survey. The request is a plain download: it sends no identifier and none of your data. As with any web request, our website's host (Vercel) sees your IP address and the app's technical identification (user agent). Announcements appear as a card in the app; an urgent one may also appear as a notification created on your phone. You can turn announcements off in Settings > Notification settings.

Purchases: prices, purchases and subscription status are handled by the App Store or Google Play.

Voice input: only if you allow your phone's online speech service (section 4).

Links you open: our website, store pages, WhatsApp, SMS and email open in other apps or your browser, under their own terms.

The app does not use any analytics, advertising, crash-reporting or tracking service.
privacyContent.subscriptionsText:
Monthly and yearly Premium are auto-renewable subscriptions sold through the Apple App Store or Google Play. When offered, a free trial is shown on the in-app paywall and in the store purchase dialog. After the trial ends, your subscription renews automatically at the plan price shown unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the trial ends in App Store → Subscriptions or Google Play → Subscriptions.

Lifetime Premium is a one-time purchase, not a subscription. We do not collect or store payment card details. Subscription status is verified only through Apple or Google.
privacyContent.howWeUseText: Your data is used only on your device, to run the app's features: reminders, the assistant, statistics and summaries. We do not sell your data, share it with anyone or use it for advertising.
privacyContent.optionalAnalyticsText: Unutma does not collect usage statistics, event logs, crash reports or analytics, and sends none of them to any server. If a screen crashes, a short technical note is kept only on your device. There are no ads in the app; the app does not use an advertising identifier or track you across other apps or websites.
privacyContent.securityText:
The vault, the journal, the assistant's stored data and the people saved for sending are encrypted on your device with AES-256. The key is kept in your phone's secure storage (Keychain on iPhone, Keystore on Android). The vault and past journal entries open with your device lock or biometrics, and screenshots are blocked while the vault is open.

Your other records (tasks, notes, lists, calendar, expenses and settings) and photos added to the journal are kept in the app's private storage. Your phone's own security protects them, but the app does not encrypt them separately.

Backup files are encrypted with AES-256, using a key derived from the password you set. Keep that password safe: we cannot recover it.
privacyContent.feedbackText: You can email us from the app: the feedback survey, the "Misunderstood" list (you can remove rows before sending) and the contact address below. In each case your own email app opens with a draft, and nothing is sent until you send it yourself. When you do, we receive what you wrote and your email address; the survey also includes your answers and the app language. We use these emails only to reply and to improve the app, do not share them, and delete them if you ask. The app may show a card inviting you to the feedback survey. If you send your answers, we may reply with a discount code; we see your email address only because you sent the email.
privacyContent.gdprRightsText: Data protection laws such as the GDPR in the EU and the UK or the KVKK in Türkiye give you rights over your personal data. Because your content stays on your device and we do not have a copy, you control it directly: you can view, change, back up and delete it in the app, and uninstalling the app removes it. For emails you have sent us, you can ask to see them or have them deleted by writing to the address below.
privacyContent.childrenText: Unutma is not intended for children under 13. We do not knowingly collect data from children.
privacyContent.policyChangesText: We may update this policy. The "Last updated" date at the top will change. Continued use of the app after changes means you accept the updated policy.

termsContent.usageText: UNUTMA is a personal productivity app for organizing routines, reminders, lists, notes, and secure data. You agree to use it only for lawful purposes and in accordance with these terms.
termsContent.subscriptionsText:
UNUTMA offers optional Premium features through in-app purchases.

In-app trial: New users may receive a 7-day in-app trial with full Premium access at no charge. This trial does not create a store subscription.

Subscriptions: Monthly and yearly Premium are auto-renewing subscriptions billed through Apple or Google. When a free trial is offered, it is shown on the paywall and in the store checkout. Unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the trial ends in App Store → Subscriptions or Google Play → Subscriptions, you will be charged automatically when the trial ends and on each renewal period.

Lifetime: The lifetime plan is a one-time purchase without recurring charges.

Cancellation and refunds: Manage or cancel subscriptions in your Apple or Google account. Refunds follow Apple or Google policies. Prices vary by region; the price shown at purchase applies.
